title: WaterChain Step 6 development holdout and adversarial validation
evaluation_type: separately authored synthetic development holdout; not independent or blinded

cases.purpose: A new clean linked transition pattern at collection.
cases.rationale: All stage records are eligible, share one batch and source, use the same analyte, and follow strict chronology.

cases.purpose: Negative source/collection/storage and positive serving result.
cases.rationale: One fully linked synthetic pathway with negative observations before the earliest positive.

cases.purpose: All linked results are not detected.
cases.rationale: No positive transition is observed; no stage attribution should be emitted.

cases.purpose: Storage has both detected and not-detected outcomes.
cases.rationale: Discordant findings at a stage should be reviewed rather than letting a positive result automatically win.

cases.purpose: Two distinct rows share a record identifier.
cases.rationale: Duplicate identifiers can indicate duplicated imports or misidentified records, so attribution must stop.

cases.purpose: Source and storage rows use the same sample ID.
cases.rationale: Distinct pathway stages must have traceable, distinct physical samples for stage comparisons.

cases.purpose: A positive record exists only on a different batch from the shared pathway.
cases.rationale: The engine should use only the unique batch linked across all four stages, not the unrelated batch's result.

cases.purpose: Every stage contains evidence for two common batch identifiers.
cases.rationale: The engine must not merge multiple possible water journeys into one transition claim.

cases.purpose: A positive storage result has an undocumented control.
cases.rationale: QC fields must explicitly pass for the result to be eligible for cross-stage inference.

cases.purpose: A positive storage result has a failed negative control.
cases.rationale: A QC failure excludes the result from inference.

cases.purpose: Source and collection timestamps are indistinguishable.
cases.rationale: Equal timestamps do not establish strict order for the conceptual pathway.

cases.purpose: A batch-associated record names a conflicting water source.
cases.rationale: Source identity conflict prevents attribution across the purported path.

cases.purpose: Only the storage record switches from presence/absence to concentration.
cases.rationale: Different analytes/results cannot be combined into one stage-transition claim.

cases.purpose: One consistent quantitative analyte, positive serving concentration, negatives upstream.
cases.rationale: The supported concentration format can be used when all stages use the same analyte and the quantitative value/unit are present.

cases.purpose: Source and downstream stages all report positive.
cases.confidence_label: observed at source; origin timing unresolved
cases.rationale: An observed source positive is not a claim that contamination originated there.
A four-stage transition cannot be discussed when one stage lacks an eligible result.

limitations: Every case is synthetic and authored by the developer; no real samples or lab results are present.
The test set is separate from the Step 5 scenario generator but is not independently blinded or externally adjudicated.
Conformance measures software behavior against hand-declared expected decisions, not real-world causal accuracy.
The rule engine does not model intermittent contamination, sample sensitivity, transfer/refill graphs, or probabilistic uncertainty.
Passing this suite does not establish safety, public-health utility, scientific validation, novelty, or superiority over other tools.
